findings.text: Status helpers adjust per-interrupt status by number: one marks noprobe, one marks nothread, one clears nothread to permit threading, one sets or clears nested thread from a boolean, and one applies a combined per-CPU devid configuration suppressing autoenable while marking per-CPU plus nothread plus noprobe plus devid.

Lookup helpers resolve a Linux interrupt number to its data record and expose the interrupt chip, direct chip pointer from a data pointer, chip private data, common handler data, message signalled descriptor, current affinity mask and effective affinity mask, returning null when no record exists.

Affinity update copies a caller mask into the common record only with multiprocessor support and otherwise does nothing; node query returns the stored node with NUMA support and zero otherwise, with a per-data wrapper delegating to the common record.

Descriptor management offers a family forwarding requested number plus search start plus count plus node with current module context to shared allocators, covering exact number, single, from a lower bound, counted ranges and device managed forms, while single release forwards to a counted release of one.
Register offset record groups six unsigned long values identifying where enable and disable live, as well as mask and acknowledge and end of interrupt and type settings for one chip type.
Chip type record pairs a complete chip object with its register offsets and a flow handler, plus a numeric trigger type and a private mask value with a pointer to shared mask storage.

Generic chip record centralises a raw spinlock with a mapped base address and optional custom 32 bit read and write hooks plus suspend and resume hooks, a base interrupt number with a count, cached mask and wake words, a type count with opaque private data, installed and spare bit words, an owning domain pointer with list linkage, trailed by a flexible array of chip types.
Mutable generic chip register and cache state is serialized by its embedded raw spinlock, and provisioning can request nested lock initialization for stacked chips through a dedicated generic flag.

Domain generic provisioning uses a runtime table holding per-chip interrupt counts and chip totals with flag clear and set masks plus generic flags plus an exit hook and flexible chip pointers, and a creation info record adding a name with flow handler and type count plus optional init and exit hooks.

Generic chip lifecycle creates a domain chip set with a build time limit of thirty two interrupts per chip, removes a domain set, releases memory, combines remove plus release into destroy with mask and flag adjustments, derives a chip type container from a data chip pointer, builds a low-bit mask saturating to all ones at thirty two, and reads or writes registers through custom hooks when present else default mapped accessors.

Poll record links into a queue and carries a state word with a scheduling weight and a callback that consumes the poll object and a budget and reports integer progress; state bit zero means scheduled and bit one means disabled.

Simulation interface reports mapping lifecycle through a request callback returning integer status for a domain plus hardware number plus private data triple and a release callback consuming the same triple without a result.

Deferred work record chains a single-call node with a callback taking the work object and a wait object for synchronization; helpers provide plain plus lazy plus hard interrupt initializers and a define macro, with an init routine assigning the callback and clearing flags.

Work items expose pending plus busy plus hard interrupt predicates over atomic flag state; polled work uses scheduled versus disabled bits; the sampled fallback configuration reports no CPU need and empty run and single actions.

Bypass pairing connects a producer record and a consumer record each holding an event object and a peer pointer; both sides offer add and delete peer operations plus stop and start hooks, with the producer additionally carrying a Linux interrupt number.

Core invokes driver supplied callbacks: poll function for budgeted polling, simulation request and release, work function for deferred execution, bypass add and delete plus stop and start on both ends, generic chip register access plus suspend and resume, platform probe for matched devices, and declared device tree or ACPI init functions.

Chip registration provides a platform probe type taking platform device and device tree node, type checking wrappers for init and probe callbacks, device tree and ACPI declaration helpers binding compatible strings or MADT subtables to callbacks, platform driver scaffolding emitting a match table plus driver with optional chip probe and suppressed bind attributes, and an empty init when the subsystem is disabled.
Invalid hardware interrupt number is all ones at unsigned long width; default distributor interrupt priority is hex A0; extended SPI base is 4096 and extended PPI base is 1056.
Generic chip option bits are init mask cache at bit zero, init nested lock at bit one, per-type mask cache at bit two, no mask at bit three, big endian IO at bit four.

Distributor register offsets are control at zero, typer at 4, IIDR at 8, typer2 at C, status at 10 hex, set and clear SPI pairs at 40 through 58 hex, group at 80, enable set at 100, enable clear at 180, pending set at 200, pending clear at 280, active set at 300, active clear at 380, priority at 400, target at 800, SGI at F00 with clear pending at F10 and set pending at F20, config at C00, group modifier at D00, nonsecure access at E00, extended group at 1000 with extended enable pending active priority and config windows at 1200 through 3000, router at 6000 and extended router at 8000, ID window at FFD0 and PIDR2 at FFE8, with distributor size 10000 hex.

Distributor control uses bit 31 for write progress, bit 8 for no SGI request, bit 6 for disable security, bit 4 for affinity routing nonsecure, bits 1 and 0 for group one A and group one enables, with single security enables at bits 1 and 0; typer reports RSS at bit 26, LPIS at 17, MBIS at 16, ESPI at 8, SPI count as low five bits plus one times 32 with extended count from bits 27 up when ESPI present; typer2 has no SGI capability at bit 8, VIL at 7 and VID in low five bits; router mode uses bit 31 clear for one and set for any; PIDR2 architecture field is top nibble of second byte with v3 as 30 hex and v4 as 40 hex; IIDR packs implementer in low 12 bits, revision in next 4, variant in next 4, product in top 8.

Redistributor offsets reuse distributor values for control status and ID registers, with IIDR at 4, typer at 8, waker at 14, set and clear LPI at 40 and 48, property and pending bases at 70 and 78, invalidate LPI at A0, invalidate all at B0 and sync at C0; redistributor control uses bits 0 through 3 for LPI enable, clear enable, involved and write progress; waker uses bit 1 for processor sleep and bit 2 for children asleep; base address cacheability spans 0 through 7 for noncacheable through writeback variants and shareability spans 0 through 2 for non, inner and outer; GICv3 priorities are unmasked E0, IRQ C0, NMI 80, PSR I marker at bit 4, with a helper mapping nanoseconds by halving and setting bit 7 and a validity check round tripping that mapping; page size encodings are 0 for 4K, 1 for 16K, 2 for 64K under mask 3.

Sampled fallback configuration makes generic domain allocation fail, domain removal and chip level work execution into no-ops, and affinity update into a no-op without multiprocessor support, so callers must handle failure or absence of effect rather than assuming success.

All number based data and mask lookups are null safe, chip type derivation assumes the data chip belongs to a generic type container, generic allocation enforces at most 32 interrupts per chip, and mask construction saturates to all ones at 32 rather than shifting beyond width.
